spec: INV-07 and FR-2.15a. e1RM = load_kg x (1 + (reps + rir) / 30), Epley over effective reps, and only for effective reps <= 12. load_kg is weight_kg, or body weight on or before the set's date plus added load for a bodyweight exercise. `expected` is null wherever the invariant refuses to guess: no RIR, no reps, no resolvable load, or more effective reps than Epley is honest over.
expectation_shape: `expected` is null, or {load_kg, effective_reps}. It is never a float: each consumer computes load_kg * (1 + effective_reps / 30) in its own arithmetic and compares that to what the core returned. A float written here would assert this file's rounding rather than the code's, and 100 x 37/30 has no exact decimal form to write.

cases.name: an ordinary set: 100 kg x 5 at RIR 2 would have been 7 reps at failure
RIR 0 is failure and is a real value, not a missing one
RIR not recorded means no e1RM, and never the RIR-0 answer (INV-03)
task 004's named case: body weight 80 kg + 20 kg x 5 at RIR 2
the same set after weighing in 4 kg heavier is a different set's input, not this one's
a bodyweight set with no body weight logged by that date has no e1RM
a blank added load on a bodyweight exercise is zero, not missing: an unweighted pull-up
a blank weight on an ordinary exercise is a load nobody recorded
no reps means nothing to estimate from
twelve effective reps is the last one Epley is asked for
thirteen effective reps is past the bound
the bound is on reps plus RIR, not on reps: 8 at RIR 5 is a thirteen-rep set
a warm-up has an e1RM; whether it counts is INV-04's separate question
a deload set has an e1RM too; INV-08 excludes it from celebration, not from arithmetic
an incomplete set is still arithmetic; completion is INV-04's question
a fractional load carries through unrounded: rounding is INV-02's job, not this one's
